newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus shares surge on buying spree.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus shares surge on buying spree.

text.p: Cyprus shares rose 1.82 percent on Wednesday after marginal declines over previous days which were signs of a market consolidation, analysts said.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index closed at 76.84 points in heavy turnover on Wednesday, compared with Friday's close of 76.05.
"There had been a consolidation on the market over the past few days," said Theodoulos Charalambides of Laiki Investments, a member of the Popular Bank Group.
Charalambides said uncertainty about tourism flows to the island this year had affected investor sentiment.
"It appears that tourism will improve over last year but investors are not yet convinced that '97 will be a better year than '96," he said.

Tourism is the eastern Mediterranean island's main money spinner, representing 21 percent of GDP. Traveller arrival figures between January and September 1996 were down by 5.8 percent on arrivals the previous year, according to official statistics.

"We expect (tourism) to be better because there are some elements which are favourable, but the market has not yet reacted" he added, referring to the high value of sterling against the Cyprus pound and the improved economic climate in Europe, Cyprus's core tourism market.

The sub index of banks closed at 87.21, dropping 0.18 percent from Friday's close while the index for approved investment closed at 64.30 from 63.54 on Friday. In contrast, the index for tourist industries closed at 61.58 points on Wednesday, down 1.73 percent from Friday.
Charalambides put the PE ratio of the market at around 15.
"That is very attractive if one takes into account that the rate of inflation in Cyprus is low," he said.
